$comment: Growth ack (#2914 fragment). Reason: #3707 fixed `audit-uat` reporting zero outstanding items for a UAT file that had three, then dropping the phase from the report entirely. Fixing the parser alone was not enough — both reviewers found independently that the fix was invisible end to end. A file that parses to zero items is now reported with `parse_gap: true` and counted in a new `summary.parse_gap_files`, but parse-gap entries carry no items, and BOTH of these workflows gated their user-visible output on `summary.total_items === 0`. audit-uat.md printed '## All Clear ... Stop here.' and progress.md suppressed its Verification Debt section, so the headline symptom — the phase vanishing — still reproduced for a reader while only the raw JSON had changed. The growth in each file is the widened gate plus the branch that actually reports the unparsed files, with their phase and path, so the reader gets the cue to go and look. Prose is the product here: these steps ARE what an executing agent reads and acts on, so a smaller form would just move the omission. #3078 review MAJOR then forced a SECOND round of growth in the same two files for the same feature, which is why this fragment is re-armed rather than joined by a duplicate (two ack sources may never name the same path). Making the parse-gap predicate status-independent was correct, but it collided with the `scanTargets` rule that archived phase dirs are deliberately NOT milestone-filtered: an archived milestone's UAT files are `complete` BY DEFINITION, so every signed-off archived phase carrying an unreadable block entered the LIVE gate. Reproduced as one live `result: pending` row plus four archived milestones each with one unparseable block yielding `total_files: 5, total_items: 1, parse_gap_files: 4` — meaning a mature project would warn on EVERY `/gsd-progress` run, permanently, about closed history no user action can clear. `summary.parse_gap_files` now counts only non-archived entries and a new `summary.archived_parse_gap_files` carries the rest, so both workflows had to grow again: each gains the rule that the live gate excludes archived entries, plus a separate clearly-marked informational report for the archived ones. That separation cannot be expressed by editing a number — it is a new reader-facing distinction between 'work to do' and 'closed history', and if the prose does not draw it the executing agent will simply merge the two back together. audit-uat.md 5582 -> 8778 (+3196), progress.md 24791 -> 26509 (+1718).

audit-uat.md.reason: #3707: the all-clear gate widens from `total_items === 0` to `total_items === 0 && parse_gap_files === 0`, and a new branch reports unparsed UAT files with phase and path. Without it the command still prints 'All Clear' for a phase whose rows it could not parse, which is the exact symptom this issue reports; +554 bytes. #3078 review MAJOR re-arms this entry with a second, larger increment: `summary.parse_gap_files` now counts LIVE (non-archived) files only, so the `initialize` step gains the rule explaining why an archived milestone's parse gap is not an all-clear blocker, the `present` step's Unparsed filter is narrowed to entries without an `archived_milestone`, and a new sibling section renders `archived_parse_gap_files` as an explicitly informational table with a Milestone column and a standing instruction never to merge those rows into the live table, never to add them to the live count, and never to let them alone suppress All Clear or drive routing. Without that added prose the executing agent has no way to tell the two populations apart in `results` — every entry carries `parse_gap: true` — and would reinstate the permanent false warning this fix removes; +1961 bytes this round

progress.md.reason: #3707: the Verification Debt section no longer gates on outstanding items alone, so a phase whose UAT rows failed to parse is surfaced as debt instead of silently absent, and the table gains a row naming the unparsed file; +315 bytes. #3078 review MAJOR re-arms this entry: Step 1.6 now also parses and tracks `summary.archived_parse_gap_files`, states explicitly that it must NOT be folded into `parse_gap_files` or into the Verification Debt gate (with the reason — an archived milestone is signed-off history, so gating on it fires the warning on every run of a mature project forever and trains the reader to ignore the next real gap), narrows the unparsed debt row to entries with no `archived_milestone`, and adds a single italic FYI line for the archived count that is barred from adding a debt row, from changing the `{N} files` heading count, and from influencing the route suggestion. The gate and the note are only one sentence apart in the output, so without the explicit prohibition they collapse into each other; +1403 bytes this round
